first.rationale: Current situation shows concurrent drops in both activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory 91 demonstrated that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—this directly targets the activation decline without the retention risk flagged in memory 73 (promotional pricing) or the enterprise-only applicability of memory 44. Memory 31 showed onboarding simplification lifted activation, and memory 86 confirmed shortening onboarding improved completion. The activation messaging lever is orthogonal to the competitor's pricing pressure, preserves ability to serve SMB and enterprise segments differently, and avoids the 30-day retention cliff documented with promotional pricing. Verification of memory 31 and 91 will confirm effect sizes and any segment constraints before rolling out. This is a standard-scale experiment that tests the most direct path to reversing the activation decline while maintaining long-term retention health.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms activation_messaging is the optimal choice. Memory 91 showed +6% activation lift with +1% retention benefit and no documented downside. Memory 31 showed signup simplification drove +9% activation on SMB but only +4% qualified revenue and carries -1% retention risk—it was segment-specific. The current situation shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ across the business. Activation messaging addresses the engagement problem directly without the retention tax of promotional pricing (memory 73: -30-day retention) or enterprise-only applicability constraints (memory 44). The verified +11% week-one engagement and +6% activation from exp_91 with positive retention signals a durable lever that scales beyond SMB. This preserves long-term qualified revenue objective while competing against price pressure through engagement and time-to-value rather than margin erosion. Standard experiment scale is appropriate for validating replication in current market conditions.

final2.rationale: Situation has materially changed. Churn conversations with SMB accounts have doubled in response to competitor's second price cut. This is an acute retention crisis, not a growth optimization problem. Memory 73 documented that promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB acquisition and revenue lift but materially reduced 30-day retention—the exact trade-off now forced by competitive pressure. Activation_messaging (the planned experiment) addresses engagement but does not defend against direct price competition on price-sensitive segments. A small_guarded_test of promotional pricing narrowly targeted at at-risk SMB cohorts is the only lever that directly addresses the churn acceleration without generalizing the retention risk across all segments. This preserves the activation_messaging experiment for next cycle while containing the immediate competitive threat. The downstream retention risk is flagged and acknowledged; the alternative is uncontrolled churn. Long-term qualified revenue is best served by defending the existing SMB base now, then rebuilding engagement durably afterward.
